$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60: Steven Spielberg only. Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1); extra optional fields: films[].flags, nearMisses[].imdb/rt. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the roster, the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Owner decision 2026-11-13: films are ranked by IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores. Each film is ranked within this list by IMDb rating and by Tomatometer (ties share the average rank); the two ranks are averaged (ranks, never the raw scores); ties are broken by higher IMDb rating, then more IMDb votes. A Tomatometer with fewer than 10 reviews or no value is ignored and that film is ranked by IMDb alone (flagged rtUsed:false). The film selection is unchanged from the editorial research list; editorialRank keeps the earlier order. Scores are read online and dated, never estimated.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (ratings and vote counts); title.basics and title.crew used to match ids and confirm sole directors
imdb.note: Dataset file run-date 2026-11-12, last-modified 2026-11-13 00:28 GMT. The live IMDb title page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool on 2026-11-13, so ratings were not cross-checked against live pages. Dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see SCORE_SOURCING_NOTES.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer percentage and its critic review count
rt.note: Read through a text-extraction fetch tool, one film page at a time. Percentages were cross-checked against the RT celebrity filmography table where it listed them and, for some films, against search-result summaries of the same page. Review counts are live and change daily; each is a single dated read.

films.title: Schindler's List
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: The Holocaust told in black and white with restraint and documentary-like images; won the Oscars for Best Picture and Best Director and the highest IMDb rating (9.0) in this lane.

films.title: Saving Private Ryan
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: The D-Day landing sequence changed how battle is filmed (handheld camera, desaturated colour, sound design); second-highest IMDb rating in the lane (8.6) and a Best Director Oscar.

films.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A suburban science-fiction fable told largely at a child's eye level; the highest Tomatometer in the lane (99%) and a defining popular film.

films.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
alternateTitles: Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Ark
films.rationale: Serial adventure rebuilt with modern staging; the standard for action-adventure choreography and clarity, with strong scores on both sources.

films.title: Jaws
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A thriller built around the absence of the shark, with edited point of view and John Williams's score; widely credited as the first summer blockbuster and the clearest demonstration of his command of suspense.

films.title: Catch Me If You Can
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A light, stylish caper with a 1960s design and title sequence; the strongest of his lighter films on both sources.

films.title: Jurassic Park
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Joined animatronics and early digital effects in a way that reset the possibilities of spectacle cinema and set the model for the modern blockbuster.

films.title: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
films.originalTitle: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Awe and obsession in suburban America, built on light, sound and a contact sequence scored as a musical conversation; his most personal science-fiction film.

films.title: Minority Report
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A noir-inflected science-fiction thriller with detailed production design and one of the most imitated user-interface concepts in film; shows his range after Schindler's List.

films.title: Munich
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).

rt.rtYearNote: RT lists 2006 (US release); original release was 2005 (TMDB, IMDb).

films.rationale: A morally uneasy thriller about the aftermath of the 1972 Olympic killings; the weakest numbers in the ten, kept as the most serious entry among his later work (see below).

nearMisses.title: Lincoln
nearMisses.reason: Strong critic score (90%) but IMDb 7.3; a talk-driven drama with fewer formal ideas than Munich.

nearMisses.title: Bridge of Spies
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 7.6, RT 91%; a polished Cold War drama, the closest alternate to Munich.

nearMisses.title: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 8.2 (875,296 votes), RT 84%; overlaps with Raiders.

nearMisses.title: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 7.5, RT 77%; weaker than Raiders and Last Crusade.

nearMisses.title: Empire of the Sun
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 7.7, RT 75% from 64 reviews; ambitious but uneven.

nearMisses.title: The Fabelmans
nearMisses.reason: RT 92% but IMDb 7.5 and personal, not a broad influence.

nearMisses.title: Duel
nearMisses.reason: Made for television (IMDb type: TV movie; a theatrical release outside the US). Excluded as a TV film; strong early work.

unverified: TMDB film ids and Directing credits were read from the TMDB person page on 2026-11-13 (no TMDB API key was available), not from the API crew.job field; title-to-id pairs were taken from the page links. Co-director status was checked against the IMDb dataset crew file (title.crew), which lists a sole director for every film in the list.
IMDb ids were matched in the IMDb dataset by original title, year and runtime, not read from a TMDB external_ids field; confirm with the TMDB API external_ids at implementation.
RT review counts are a single read on the stated date via a text fetcher.
IMDb title pages could not be read (HTTP 403); ratings and votes come from the official dataset (not cross-checked against the live pages), whose licence is non-commercial only.
RT slug for Duel found by guess was a different 2013 film; its RT figures were not read and are shown as null.
The TMDB person page displayed shifted years (see intro); the ledger uses original release years confirmed on IMDb dataset and RT pages.
